text:
elle: I want to reopen the split control-plane / data-plane idea. sketch a pragmatic pattern for residency + failover that avoids per-request CP RPCs.
sam: good call. goals: no sync CP call on hot path, auditable decisions, quick revocation when tenant moves, and predictable degradation.
raju: prototype we ran: CP issues short-lived signed "residency assertions" (signed JWT-like blob). regional proxy caches them and enforces. no per-request CP trip.
elle: quick example of assertion we used?
raju: kept it tiny so headers stay small: 
```
{
  "aid": "assert-7f3a",
  "tenant": "t-123",
  "regions": ["eu-west-1"],
  "iat": 1680000000,
  "exp": 1680000600,
  "sig": "base64sig"
}
```
proxy verifies sig, caches until exp, and sets X-Residency-AID for logs.
megan: from compliance: we need to link each inference request to the exact assertion version and to the signing key rotation id. logs must be immutable and exportable.
sam: ops pattern: store (aid -> assertion + key_id) in CP audit DB; proxy logs aid, key_id, region and request id. that satisfies auditability.
elle: cutover: tenant changes allowed regions. safe flow?
raju: recommended flow: 1) CP creates new assertion (A2) and publishes to region caches, 2) CP marks A1 as "draining" (still valid but deprioritized), 3) proxy accepts A2 preferentially; during overlap proxies include which assert served, 4) after overlap and audit window CP revokes A1.
sam: revocation != immediate deny. use revocation flag with short grace window to account for replication slack. also use monotonic assertion ids so logs can show progression.
megan: what about keys? rotating signing keys is required quarterly. need key_id in assertion and KMS audit logs mapped to release tickets.
elle: failure modes: cache miss and CP unreachable => what should proxy do?
raju: per-tenant fallback policy: default-deny is safest. but we should support "critical allow" opt-ins for customers that accept risk. configure at tenant-level in assertion metadata.
sam: implementation notes: - keep assertions <= 1kb so they fit in headers - use TTL jittered refresh - use exponential backoff for CP pulls - expose per-tenant CP-replication-lag metric to SLO dashboards
megan: product/legal: we must surface to customers when their requests may have been served outside chosen region during a failover. propose an event stream for customers with timestamps + aids.
elle: what about active/active writes for embeddings store? residency assertions solve routing, but data replication still tricky. write recommendations?
raju: prefer primary-writes-by-residency with async replication. for compliance-bound tenants, enable single-region write-only mode and queue background replication under admin control. for others, multi-primary with conflict-free replication is OK.
sam: add a failover guard: when promoting a standby region, CP must issue a special promotion assertion signed by two control-plane leaders (2PL) to reduce accidental promotions. proxies only accept promotion assertions with dual-signature.
megan: noted. dual-signature + KMS audit will appease legal. also retention for assertion history: keep 2 years for EU customers.
elle: ops playbook items?
raju: - CP replication pipe must have per-tenant alerts when last-known assertion age > 30s - proxy cache eviction metric and guardrails - ability to force-fetch assertion for a tenant on proxy restart
sam: dev note: put assertion verification in fast path with optimized signature checks (ED25519 verified with cache of public keys) to keep latency <1ms.
megan: anything on telemetry for post-incident analysis?
elle: require 3-tuple logs: request_id, assertion_aid, key_id. plus region served and CP-published timestamp. store in immutable blobstore for 90 days by default.
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: residency-assertions v0.3 rolled to canary in eu-west-1 at 2025-03-12T18:22:00Z :rocket:
sam: next steps: write an RFC describing assertion format, lifecycle, revocation semantics, and dual-sign promotion. assign owners for KMS mappings and audit export.
elle: agree. I'll draft RFC and ping security & legal for key/retention requirements.
megan: cc: please include sample customer-facing disclosure for failover behaviour.
raju: i'll add proxy impl notes and a small test harness for assertion replication chaos tests.
elle: great, thanks all.
